⚡️⚡️🇾🇪🇮🇶🇸🇦 Earlier today, UAVs targeted two Saudi Arabia's East-West Crude Oil Pipeline, causing major damage to at least two pumping stations. One near al-Mesba'ah was hit, and another near al-Dhekra was hit.
Saudi Ministry of Foreign Affairs reports the UAVs originated from Iraq, and reports by both Saudi and U.S. officials to media outlets corroborate this claim.
The East-West pipeline has been entirely shut down by this attack, disrupting the transit of 7 million barrels of crude oil per day.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
⚡️🇺🇸🇾🇪 Anthropic says Yemen-based actors (most likely Ansar-Allah) used Claude to develop guided weapons
Anthropic says it identified a group of threat actors in northern Yemen that used Claude Code to develop software for guided weapons, including a guided rocket, a ballistic missile programme and a missile variant involving a hypersonic glide vehicle.
The company said the actors used multiple Claude instances for coding, research and code review, while attempting to evade safeguards by hiding their goals and splitting work across sessions.
Anthropic said its safeguards blocked many requests, but not all. The group eventually test-fired a guided rocket, which appears to have failed, and returned to Claude to investigate the failure.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Russian observers report Ukrainian FP-1 long-range drones moving toward Berezniki in Russia's Perm region, where a suspected attack on a chemical facility is underway. The city hosts Uralchem's Azot plant, a major producer of ammonia, nitric acid and ammonium nitrate. Investigative reporting and railway data have linked its shipments to Russian defense manufacturers including the Sverdlov explosives plant, Biysk Oleum Plant and Perm Gunpowder Plant.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Ukraine launched a combined drone and missile attack on Volgograd overnight. Multiple sources claim drones and FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles were used. Regional governor Andrey Bocharov confirmed an "industrial enterprise" in southern Volgograd was affected, while "debris" was also reported in the area. The Volgograd oil refinery is suspected to have been the target, but this has not been confirmed.

events.text: ❗️Ukrainian drones attacked the Saratov oil refinery in Russia, a Rosneft facility that has been targeted several times before. The plant can process up to 7 million tonnes of crude oil annually, around 2.2% of Russia's total refining capacity. It produces gasoline, diesel and fuel oil, and directly supplies fuel and lubricants to the Russian Armed Forces and military-industrial complex.

🤥👽🗣 Just in time to distract from Epstein, Iran dumpster fires: Trump reportedly plans big ‘aliens’ reveal
 
Trump is reportedly “sitting on a finished speech confirming humanity isn’t alone” in the universe, and the US government is gradually setting the stage for disclosure day, Wired reports.
From hints by his officials that the administration is treating the issue with the utmost seriousness, to fan service to UFO enthusiasts via a trickle of videos and docs on mysterious flying objects (five batches and counting), [to congressional hearings](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73321) and priming of the public through media, celebrities and Hollywood (Spielberg’s new Disclosure Day movie), something [‘big’ may be on the horizon](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70870).
In August, GOP megadonor and UFO enthusiast Robert Bigelow said he met with Trump and personally saw an excerpt from his aliens speech, reading: “A non-human, intelligent presence has been on Earth for a very long time, using spacecraft and with performances completely beyond our capabilities and our human physics.”
Trump has reportedly also told members of his inner circle there are aliens living in the Earth’s oceans.
That’s all well and good, but why now? What could possibly be going on in the world that requires [an urgent distraction](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/61356)? [The Middle East and Eastern Europe on fire](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74410)? Check. [Energy prices skyrocketing](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73674)? Check. US debt on the brink of a potentially irreversible calamity? Check. Global elites implicated in a monstrous child abuse scandal? Big check. Quick: release the little green men!
In 1958, Soviet-Russian sci-fi author Ivan Efremov speculated on humanity’s first contact with an alien lifeform, concluding that this could take place only between civilizations that had resolved all the economic and social contradictions on their home planets to reach for the stars.
Look around – does our world look anything like it’s anywhere close? Why would aliens want to hang out with an orange man-child [threatening to wipe out whole civilizations](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73029), anyway?

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇸🇦⚔️ Why Saudi Arabia stands alone as Houthi strikes test the Mecca Pact
In August 2026, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey signed a joint defense pact in Mecca: an attack on one is an attack on all. Today, Saudi Arabia is under Houthi missile and drone strikes. Its partners, however, are in no hurry to fight—and the US, its traditional ally, now limits itself to arms supplies and intelligence, avoiding direct combat.
Turkey has not committed to fighting for Saudi Arabia. It competes with Riyadh for leadership in the Islamic world, and the Red Sea crisis benefits Ankara: 12–15% of global trade and nearly 30% of container traffic to Europe passes through Bab-el-Mandeb, and any disruption hits Saudi and UAE ports hardest. Turkey poses as a "mediator," strengthening influence while rivals lose logistical advantages. It has officially condemned Houthi attacks but will not join strikes. Iran, backing the Houthis, could also strike Turkish interests in Syria. Helping Saudi Arabia means stabilizing a competitor.
Pakistan is cautious of getting involved as an estimated 15–20% of its population is Shia—the second-largest Shia population after Iran. War against fellow believers risks interconfessional tensions. Officially, Islamabad cites the pact's defensive nature and demands "additional "mechanisms"—diplomatic language for indefinite postponement. Defense Minister Khawaja Asif has made harsher statements than the Foreign Ministry, revealing internal divergence. Pakistan's fragile economy is also at risk.
The US avoids being a belligerent. Over 100 American military advisers are in Saudi Arabia providing targeting and intelligence, but no direct strikes or aerial refueling. After more than six months of war with Iran, the US military is exhausted, with focus shifted to the Strait of Hormuz. The White House formula: give partners capabilities, not fight for them.
